builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
summary: WebHarbor replaces live-website evaluation and low-fidelity synthetic environments with 153 dockerized, deterministic reconstructions of real web services covering 3,518 tasks including authenticated workflows. The cost is substantial environment-construction effort via human-agent collaboration and the infrastructure to run many containerized sites, plus RL training that, while feasible at 4B scale, still demands GPU-hours beyond a minimal budget. What can fail is a fidelity gap between replicas and live sites (agents may overfit to simplified or outdated reproductions) and continued divergence as real services evolve.
rationale: The reader cannot justify building or maintaining 153 dockerized site replicas, but should track the released suite as a potential future evaluation and RL resource for small-scale GUI agents.
technique: Dockerized high-fidelity website replicas for GUI-agent RL

claims.statement: WebHarbor replaces live-website evaluation and low-fidelity synthetic environments with 153 dockerized, deterministic reconstructions of real web services covering 3,518 tasks including authenticated workflows. The cost is substantial environment-construction effort via human-agent collaboration and the infrastructure to run many containerized sites, plus RL training that, while feasible at 4B scale, still demands GPU-hours beyond a minimal budget. What can fail is a fidelity gap between replicas and live sites (agents may overfit to simplified or outdated reproductions) and continued divergence as real services evolve.

A Qwen 4B-level GUI agent trained with RL in WebHarbor is reported to generalize to unseen tasks and perform competitively with leading open-source GUI web agents across four benchmarks; no multiplicative factor is stated.
